name: Crestfield Consumer Brands
about: A national grocery and drug retailer buying packaged goods from roughly 1,400 suppliers into eleven distribution centres.
sourceDoc: Crestfield EDI Implementation Guide v4.2 (PDF, January 2024)

envelope.senderNote: Your 9-digit DUNS, left justified, space filled to 15.
envelope.usageNote: T during certification, P once Crestfield confirms production cutover in writing. Sending P before cutover routes your transaction into a queue nobody watches.

contacts.name: Crestfield EDI Support
contacts.note: Transmission failures and 997 queries. Monday to Friday, 7am to 7pm Eastern.

contacts.name: Crestfield Supplier Enablement
contacts.note: Certification scheduling and DC routing guides.

commonRules.statement: ISA15 must be T until Crestfield confirms production cutover in writing, and P thereafter.
commonRules.rationale: Production transactions sent during certification are not monitored, and test transactions sent after cutover are not received.

commonRules.statement: Crestfield returns a 997 within 60 minutes of receiving an interchange. No 997 after 60 minutes should be treated as a transmission failure on your side.
commonRules.rationale: A silent failure is the most common reason a supplier believes a document was sent when Crestfield never received it.

name: Halverson Motors
about: A vehicle manufacturer running three assembly plants on sequenced just-in-time supply, buying from roughly 600 tier one suppliers.
sourceDoc: Halverson Motors Supplier EDI Standard, Revision 11 (PDF, September 2025)

envelope.senderNote: Your DUNS. Halverson does not accept mutually defined (ZZ) qualifiers.
envelope.usageNote: T throughout the test phase. Halverson schedules production cutover per plant, so a supplier may be P for one plant and T for another during a phased launch.

maintenanceWindow: 23:00 to 04:00 plant local, nightly, for the MRP run

contacts.name: Halverson EDI Helpdesk
contacts.note: 24 hours during production, excluding plant shutdown weeks.

commonRules.statement: Every transaction must carry the Halverson supplier code in REF*ZZ at header level.
commonRules.rationale: The DUNS in the envelope identifies the corporate entity; the supplier code identifies the shipping location, and Halverson routes on the latter.

commonRules.statement: Cumulative quantities are reset annually on 1 January. A cumulative figure carried across the year boundary will not reconcile.
commonRules.rationale: Halverson closes cumulative accounting at year end, and a carried figure produces a false overship.

commonRules.statement: Halverson returns a 997 within 30 minutes. Transmission windows close at 23:00 plant local time and reopen at 04:00.
commonRules.rationale: The overnight window is reserved for the MRP run, and transmissions during it queue rather than process.

name: Northwind Grocery Group
about: A regional grocery chain of 340 stores with four distribution centres and a large direct store delivery programme.
sourceDoc: Northwind Trading Partner Guidelines v7.1 (PDF, March 2025)

envelope.senderNote: DUNS, or DUNS plus 4 for suppliers with multiple shipping points.
envelope.usageNote: T until Northwind confirms production in writing. Northwind runs a two week parallel period during which both T and P are accepted.

commonRules.statement: Northwind is on 005010. Transactions at 004010 are rejected at the group level.
commonRules.rationale: Northwind migrated in 2024 and does not maintain a 004010 translator.

commonRules.statement: Catch weight items must carry actual weight, not nominal. Nominal weight on a variable weight item produces an invoice discrepancy at receipt.
commonRules.rationale: Random weight product is received by weight and invoiced by weight.

name: Vantage Logistics Group
about: An asset-light 3PL tendering freight to roughly 900 carriers and operating eleven contract warehouses for shipper clients.
sourceDoc: Vantage Carrier and Warehouse EDI Specification v9 (PDF, November 2025)

envelope.senderNote: Carriers use their SCAC. Warehouse operators use the Vantage site code.
envelope.usageNote: T during onboarding. Vantage certifies per lane for carriers and per site for warehouses.

maintenanceWindow: None. Freight moves overnight, so the interface does not close.

commonRules.statement: Times are local to the event location and must carry the time zone in the time code element where the segment provides one.
commonRules.rationale: A status without a zone cannot be ordered against other events, and Vantage operates across four zones.

commonRules.statement: Vantage returns a 997 within 15 minutes. Transmissions are accepted 24 hours a day with no maintenance window.
commonRules.rationale: Freight moves overnight, so the interface does not close.

name: Pallas Health System
about: An integrated delivery network of 22 hospitals and 140 clinics, buying medical and surgical supplies through a consolidated service centre.
sourceDoc: Pallas Supplier Integration Guide, 2026 Edition (PDF, December 2025)

envelope.senderNote: DUNS. Pallas also accepts GLN (qualifier UL) for suppliers standardised on GS1.
envelope.usageNote: T until Pallas confirms production. Pallas certifies per transaction set, not per supplier, so you may be live on 850 while still testing 856.

contacts.name: Pallas Item Data Team
contacts.note: GTIN, UOM and contract price alignment.

commonRules.statement: Every item must be identified by GTIN. Pallas does not accept supplier catalogue numbers as the sole identifier on any transaction.
commonRules.rationale: Pallas standardised on GS1 in 2024, and recall management depends on a single item identity across every document.

commonRules.statement: Lot number and expiry date are required for every item subject to recall or dating, on both the ASN and the invoice.
commonRules.rationale: Recall response time is a patient safety measure and a regulatory obligation, and it depends on lot traceability at receipt.

commonRules.statement: Pallas returns a 997 within one hour, and an 824 for business validation on 850, 856 and 810.
commonRules.rationale: Two stage validation means an accepted 997 does not confirm the document was usable.

name: Meridian Industrial Supply
about: A distributor of maintenance, repair and operations supplies serving manufacturing plants, with 2,800 suppliers and a large drop-ship programme.
sourceDoc: Meridian Supplier EDI Requirements v5.3 (PDF, April 2026)

envelope.senderNote: DUNS. Drop-ship suppliers use the same DUNS as their stocking relationship.
envelope.usageNote: T during certification. Meridian certifies stocking and drop-ship flows separately because the ship-to differs.

contacts.name: Meridian Direct Fulfilment
contacts.note: End customer address and delivery questions.

commonRules.statement: Drop-ship transactions must carry the end customer in N1*ST and Meridian in N1*BY. Reversing these ships product to the wrong address.
commonRules.rationale: Roughly 40 percent of Meridian volume ships directly to the end customer, and the ship-to is not Meridian.

commonRules.statement: Meridian returns a 997 within two hours and operates a nightly maintenance window from 02:00 to 03:00 Central.
commonRules.rationale: Transmissions during the window queue and process at 03:00.

name: Brightline Apparel
about: A specialty apparel retailer with 620 stores and an e-commerce operation, buying from roughly 300 vendors, most of them importing.
sourceDoc: Brightline Vendor Routing and EDI Manual, 2026 (PDF, May 2026)

envelope.senderNote: Brightline uses phone-number qualifier 12 for historical reasons. Your assigned ID is on your vendor setup sheet, not your DUNS.
envelope.usageNote: T during testing. Brightline requires a successful parallel of all five transaction sets before any goes to production.

commonRules.statement: Every style must be identified by the Brightline style, colour and size combination. A style number alone is not sufficient on any transaction.
commonRules.rationale: Apparel is bought and sold at the size and colour level, and a style-level transaction cannot be allocated to a store.

commonRules.statement: Vendor compliance chargebacks are applied monthly against the standards in the routing manual, not against this guide alone.
commonRules.rationale: The routing manual covers physical packing and labelling, which EDI cannot express.

commonRules.statement: Brightline returns a 997 within four hours. The EDI interface is unavailable Sunday 02:00 to 06:00 Eastern for maintenance.
commonRules.rationale: The weekly window is used for item master and allocation processing.

name: Cobalt Energy Services
about: An oilfield and midstream services operator buying equipment, consumables and contracted field labour across four basins.
sourceDoc: Cobalt Energy Supplier EDI and Invoicing Standard v3 (PDF, June 2026)

envelope.senderNote: DUNS at the legal entity that holds the master service agreement.
envelope.usageNote: T until Cobalt confirms production per transaction set.

ackWindow: 997 within 4 hours, 824 on failed invoice validation

commonRules.statement: Every transaction must carry the authorisation for expenditure number in REF*AH and the cost centre in REF*CC.
commonRules.rationale: Cobalt allocates all spend to a well or facility, and a transaction with no AFE cannot be coded or approved.

commonRules.statement: Cobalt returns a 997 within four hours, and an 824 on invoices that fail business validation.
commonRules.rationale: Invoice validation runs against the field ticket and the AFE, and takes longer than syntax checking.
